claims.text: The initial material is a single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy.
The intervention introduces a secondary phase consisting of Co-rich nanoparticles.
Annealing at 500 °C for 1 hour will induce precipitation of Co-rich nanoparticles.
Co-rich nanoparticles will pin magnetic domain walls.
Co-rich nanoparticles will reduce magnetic domain size.
Domain-wall pinning by the Co-rich nanoparticles will increase coercive field.
The modified alloy will have a coercive field at least 50% higher than single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
The coercive field of the single-phase fcc FeCoNi baseline is 100 Oe.
The intervention will raise coercive field from 100 Oe to at least 150 Oe.
The hypothesis is scoped to FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys having an fcc matrix and potential secondary phases.
Coercivity is to be evaluated using magnetic hysteresis-loop measurements.
The modified sample is to be compared with a single-phase fcc FeCoNi control.
TEM or SEM will be used to assess the modified microstructure.
The hypothesis is falsified if the modified sample does not show a significant coercivity increase above 100 Oe relative to the control.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 50% increase, from 100 Oe to 150 Oe, whereas the falsification rule only requires a significant value above 100 Oe. An outcome between 100 and 150 Oe could fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
